title: Almost Sure Convergence Rates of Stochastic Approximation and Reinforcement Learning via a Poisson-Moreau Drift
abstract: arXiv:2605.07104v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Establishing almost sure convergence rates for stochastic approximation and reinforcement learning under Markovian noise is a fundamental theoretical challenge. We make progress towards this challenge for a class of stochastic approximation algorithms whose expected updates are contractive, a setting that arises in many reinforcement learning algorithms such as $Q$-learning and linear temporal difference learning. Specifically, for a power-law learning rate $O(n^{-\eta})$ with $\eta \in (1/2, 1)$, we obtain an almost sure convergence rate arbitrarily close to $o(n^{1 - 2\eta})$. For the harmonic learning rate $\alpha_n=\alpha/(n+1)$, the almost sure squared-error rate is $o(n^{-\zeta})$ for every $\zeta<\min\{1,2(1-\kappa)\alpha\}$, where $\kappa$ is the contraction factor. Thus exponents arbitrarily close to one are available when $2(1-\kappa)\alpha\geq1$. This approaches the $n^{-1}$ polynomial exponent of classical law-of-the-iter

translated_title: 基于泊松-莫罗漂移的随机逼近与强化学习的几乎必然收敛速率
translated_abstract: 在马尔可夫噪声下建立随机逼近和强化学习的几乎必然收敛速率是一个根本性的理论挑战。我们为一类期望更新具有压缩性质的随机逼近算法在这一挑战上取得了进展，该设置出现在许多强化学习算法中，例如Q学习和线性时序差分学习。具体而言，对于幂律学习率O(n^(-η))（其中η ∈ (1/2, 1)），我们获得了可任意接近o(n^(1-2η))的几乎必然收敛速率。对于调和学习率α_n=α/(n+1)，对于每个ζ<min{1,2(1-κ)α}，几乎必然平方误差速率为o(n^(-ζ))，其中κ为压缩因子。因此，当2(1-κ)α≥1时，可获得任意接近1的指数。这接近了经典迭代对数定律（原文截断）……的n^(-1)多项式指数。
tldr: 本文通过泊松-莫罗漂移技术，为马尔可夫噪声下期望更新具有压缩性的随机逼近算法（如Q学习和线性时序差分学习）建立了几乎必然收敛速率，在幂律学习率下获得了可任意接近o(n^(1-2η))的速率，在调和学习率下当参数满足条件时平方误差指数可任意接近1。
en_tdlr: Via a Poisson-Moreau drift, this paper establishes almost sure convergence rates for stochastic approximation algorithms with contractive expected updates (arising in Q-learning and linear TD learning) under Markovian noise, achieving rates arbitrarily close to o(n^(1-2η)) for power-law learning rates and squared-error exponents arbitrarily close to one for harmonic learning rates under suitable conditions.
